<!-- fcagentic-unit-challenge: practical -->

## 1. Define the scenario and outcome

Give a self-contained interesting goal and explain what the learner will produce.

## 2. Predict an ordinary run

Supply example inputs, outputs, and an observable trajectory. Name success,
termination, budgets, allowed tools, and forbidden actions.

## 3. Start from the contract

Provide the public signatures, schema, synthetic data, or partial structure needed
to start without revealing the central decisions. Include a non-agentic baseline.

## 4. Build in small stages

Stage ordinary behavior, the important boundary, and injected failure recovery.
Ask for one controlled change and its expected downstream effects.

## 5. Run progressive assertions

Supply executable independent assertions. Separate deterministic contract checks
from repeated model evaluation. Do not require a network service or paid account.

## 6. Use the hint ladder only when needed

<details>
<summary>Hint 1: locate the failing boundary</summary>
Replace with a question that focuses attention without giving the answer.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2: compare state before and after the action</summary>
Replace with a direction grounded in the actual scenario.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3: complete a partial scaffold</summary>
Supply the smallest useful partial implementation.
</details>

## 7. Keep debugging evidence

Record expected versus actual behavior, the earliest failure, one change, the
regression check, and a limitation. Keep secrets and private reasoning out.

<details>
<summary>One solution path and its trade-offs</summary>
Supply a complete tested solution with ordinary, boundary, and injected-fault checks.
</details>

<!-- Add an artifact-specific JSON quiz and OJS include here before publication. -->

## 8. Record your retrospective

Explain whether the agent improved on its baseline. Preserve measured quality,
latency/cost where applicable, failed assumptions, and an architecture decision.
